question: Given a representative read-only audit still reached no_progress after repeated search/read calls, which bounded slice can close the exploration loop without changing execution semantics?

confirmed_facts.fact: NotebookLM's current vision prioritizes transparent progress, bounded exploration, honest stopping, and visible handoff over hidden model self-report.
The read-only graph removed write tools, but the generic BASE_SYSTEM and durable exploration nudge still instructed the model to seek edit/write actions.

Before the nudge correction, the real-config read-only audit produced a final three-finding handoff only after 13 steps and manifest halt_reason no_progress; after the correction it approved in 7 steps with three path-qualified findings.

contradictions: NotebookLM's heuristic OVER-BRANCHING HUD alert would infer model behavior from counters and risks false positives; exact deterministic counters already surface the observable condition.
A physical-signal inertia HUD would duplicate existing bounded progress diagnostics and can falsely label legitimate read-only work as stalled.
Extracting milestones from model Markdown plans would trust self-report, contrary to the project's deterministic verification boundary.

unverified_hypotheses.hypothesis: A bounded read-only runtime prompt and mode-safe durable nudge will make inspection tasks stop after enough evidence instead of pursuing unavailable writes.
support: local trace showed unavailable write instruction in read-only context
against: prompt compliance alone is not a hard execution guarantee
unverified_hypotheses.experiment: Run the real user config with --read-only and a representative TUI audit; require approved manifest and concise path-qualified findings.

candidates.core: read-only runtime prompt plus mode-safe exploration nudge

local_adjudication.reason: The existing exact stall/error/explore counters expose the deterministic condition without guessing model intent.
Useful only if a concrete telemetry gap is reproduced; current read-only smoke needs a stopping contract, not another warning.
It would weaken the maker/checker boundary by treating model narration as completion evidence.

local_adjudication.candidate: read-only runtime prompt plus mode-safe exploration nudge
local_adjudication.reason: Local trace identified the unavailable-write contradiction; after removing it, real-config smoke approved in 7 steps with three concise findings.

implementation.core: Build a read-only-specific system prompt, route it only through read-only graph assembly, and make the durable exploration nudge request finish/reporting rather than unavailable writes.
constraints: keep BASE_SYSTEM and write-enabled behavior unchanged
keep MAX_EXPLORE and deterministic verification unchanged
do not add hidden-reasoning heuristics, new state machine, provider, MCP, or langgraph semantics
validation: real-config --read-only smoke: approved=true, 7 steps, three path-qualified findings
BusyFixture + ResizeProbe and StressFixture + InspectAnswer ConPTY regressions passed

recommendation: Accept the read-only contract slice; reject the three speculative NLM candidates and retain the current notes as the vision and completed-history record.

next_step.value: Archive this verified iteration and reconcile the current completed Note; next usability slice requires a fresh reproduced pain.

stop_conditions: Do not add heuristic model-intent alerts without a concrete false-negative/false-positive trace.
Do not parse model self-report as deterministic completion evidence.
Do not claim broad project completion from this single read-only smoke; keep the iteration goal active for future NLM-guided slices.
